ScheduledTaskDTO.title: ScheduledTaskDTO
ScheduledTaskDTO.description:
A registered background task definition, as returned by the API.

Mirrors ``ScheduledTaskEntity`` 1:1 plus two derived fields the UI
needs: ``next_run_at`` (already a native column, included here for
from_attributes symmetry) and ``last_run`` — the most recent
``TaskRunEntity`` for this task, embedded to avoid a second
round-trip from the tasks overview page.

params.title: Params
params.description: Full replacement for the task's params, not a merge/patch: when present, this dict entirely overwrites the stored params.

ScheduledTaskUpdateDTO.title: ScheduledTaskUpdateDTO
ScheduledTaskUpdateDTO.description:
Partial update body for ``PATCH /tasks/{task_id}``.

All fields are optional; only the ones present in the request body
are applied (see ``model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`` in the router).
``schedule_cron`` and ``schedule_interval_seconds`` are mutually
exclusive by construction: setting one non-null in the *resulting*
task state nulls the other, and a request that sets both non-null at
once is rejected with 422.

SendRequest.title: SendRequest
SendRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /mail/send``.

Mirrors the gateway's ``SendRequest`` and adds an optional cockpit
``ticket_number`` that is stripped before forwarding.

Timings.title: Timings
Timings.description:
Per-turn latency breakdown in milliseconds.

A **projection**, not a storage schema: assembled at read time from the
``call_metrics`` rows belonging to a turn. Never persisted in
``calls.history``.

``llm_ms`` and ``tool_ms`` are siblings that sum, both totalled over the
turn because one turn can make several LLM round-trips interleaved with
tool calls. ``agent_ms`` encloses both, so ``agent_ms - llm_ms - tool_ms``
is SDK and framework overhead.

``tts_first_byte_ms`` is merged in from the ``tts`` metric row rather than
measured by the turn clock — TTS reports its own first-byte latency, and
on the SIP path that instant is not observable from Python at all.
``to_audio_out_ms`` therefore spans "agent finished" to "audio playing"
and includes synthesis.
